speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help determine the cause of your double vision and weakness, can you tell me if these symptoms fluctuate throughout the day, often worsening with fatigue or towards evening?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you, that pattern of fatigability is very characteristic. I would like to examine your eyes now; do you notice any drooping of your eyelids, or have you experienced any difficulty with swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, so the weakness is symmetrical and there is no family history, which helps narrow it down. Do you have any difficulty with chewing or swallowing, and have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of swallowing or breathing difficulties is reassuring, but the fluctuating weakness and ocular symptoms still strongly suggest a neuromuscular junction disorder. I would like to order a blood test for acetylcholine receptor antibodies to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_Receptor_Antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated acetylcholine receptor antibodies, combined with your fluctuating weakness and double vision, confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis
